Headline: "There is some room for movement on tax, says Burnham".
In an LBC interview, Burnham said there is "some room" for movement on tax; suggested business rates on warehouses could rise to fund tax cuts for pubs and some high-street businesses.
Quotes (Burnham): "I stick by the manifesto and the promises that it made... So, let me be absolutely clear about that, but there is some room within that manifesto for movement on tax."
Pubs, clubs and music venues would receive a 20% cut; smaller independent hospitality/leisure/retail would have the business-rates threshold raised for the first time since 2017.
On welfare, Burnham said he would not make "crude cuts to benefit levels that just put people who are struggling in even worse poverty"; instead reduce the benefits bill via education changes, technical qualifications, work placements for 16-year-olds and mental-health support.
Badenoch (Conservative) accused him of "running away from being asked questions."

Cross-ref (BBC cy9rgg9ddw2o, 2026-07-01): "Badenoch accuses Starmer of leaving defence spending 'mess' for Burnham" — Badenoch cited a c.£5bn shortfall in the Defence Investment Plan; Burnham told about a £4.7bn defence funding gap; next chancellor will have to "find the resources" in the autumn Budget.

The Times interview (thetimes.com, reported): Burnham said he had already spoken to the Treasury about planned announcements and stressed making people "feel better"; frozen tax thresholds "lodged in his mind"; "The breathing space point is a really serious one."
